title: Stabilization of bulk quantum orders in finite Rydberg atom arrays
abstract: Addresses a fundamental challenge in Rydberg atom array experiments: theoretical bulk quantum phases diverge from experimental realizations on finite-sized arrays due to strong boundary effects. Proposes a general, experimentally straightforward strategy to mitigate boundary effects by leveraging the disordered phase in Rydberg systems to drive boundaries into configurations determined by bulk physics. Numerically demonstrated in one- and two-dimensional systems for both ordered and critical phases. Over 200 atoms now reliably exhibit bulk-like quantum order, compared to previous limits of approximately 50 atoms.
key_claims: Boundary effects suppressed using disordered-phase regions at array edges
Protocol works for both ordered and critical bulk phases in 1D and 2D
200+ atom arrays now reliably show bulk-like quantum order (was ~50 atoms before)
Experimentally straightforward — no exotic controls required
Directly addresses a known failure mode in finite Rydberg MERA implementations
supports_or_contradicts: SUPPORTS — directly addresses the boundary pathology that plagued our HYP-017 validator attempts (15- and 20-atom geometries showed boundary-dominated behavior). This protocol could allow smaller test arrays to exhibit bulk holographic behavior, potentially resurrecting a reduced-scale validator approach.
